Win probability and expected survivors for a battle

Source: R/battle.R
rk_battle_odds.Rd

Computes the probability that the attacker conquers the territory, together with the expected surviving armies on both sides. The default "mc" method simulates n independent battles; "exact" solves the absorbing Markov chain over army states and involves no simulation.

Usage

rk_battle_odds(
  att_armies,
  def_armies,
  n = 10000L,
  max_def = 2L,
  method = c("mc", "exact")
)

Arguments

att_armies

Number of armies on the attacking territory (must be >= 2, since one army must remain behind).

def_armies

Number of armies on the defending territory (>= 1).

n

Number of simulated battles. Ignored when method = "exact".

max_def

Maximum defender dice permitted (default 2L).

method

Either "mc" (Monte Carlo, the default) or "exact".

Value

A one-row tibble::tibble() with columns:

att_armies, def_armies

integer, the starting armies.

method

character, "mc" or "exact".

n

integer, the number of simulated battles; NA_integer_ for the exact method.

p_conquer

double, probability that the attacker takes the territory.

e_att_survivors, e_def_survivors

double, expected armies left on the attacking and defending territory when the battle ends.

See also

Other combat: rk_battle(), rk_duel(), rk_duel_dist(), rk_duel_odds(), rk_odds_table()

Examples

# Exact, no simulation
rk_battle_odds(10, 8, method = "exact")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors
#>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1         10          8 exact     NA     0.646            4.05            1.23

set.seed(1)
rk_battle_odds(10, 8, n = 500)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors
#>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1         10          8 mc       500     0.588            3.74            1.46
